A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same 3DTrajMaster work, with complete, readable main text and appendices A–F. Their equations, tables, figures, and supplementary examples can be matched reliably.

before.justification: V1 reports original trajectory-control evaluations, ablations, qualitative generation results, and a 53-sample user-preference survey, including Tables 2–3 and R8–R12.

after.justification: V2 retains the same original quantitative experiments, qualitative results, ablations, and user-preference survey in the main text and appendices.

M1.justification: The pose encoder, entity–trajectory fusion, gated attention, LoRA domain adaptor, training objectives, and annealed sampling remain unchanged in Section 3, Algorithm 1, and Appendix A.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 360°-Motion training dataset and single- and multiple-entity evaluation scenarios. The entity categories, environments, and supplementary analysis of Artgrid, Pixabay, and Pexels are unchanged.

E2.justification: Table 2 retains Base T2V, MotionCtrl, Tora, and Direct-a-Video. The qualitative comparisons and Table R12 user-preference comparisons also retain their respective comparator sets.

E3.justification: Training budgets, inference settings, evaluation metrics, and pose-estimation procedures are identical. Both retain 100 evaluation pairs comprising 12 single-, 72 two-, and 16 three-entity cases, alongside the same appendix protocols.

E4.justification: Section 4.6 and Appendix F retain identical analyses of fusion design, domain adaptation, annealed sampling, hyperparameter sensitivity, negative pose conditioning, and entity editing. No analysis or case study is added or removed.

E5.justification: Statistical reporting is unchanged, including the point estimates and user-preference percentages. No repeated-run, seed, confidence-interval, or significance-testing information is added or revised.

E6.justification: All numerical entries and qualitative examples match. For example, Table 2 retains 3DTrajMaster's all-entity TransErr of 0.398 and RotErr of 0.277; Tables 3 and R8–R12 are also unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical task formulation, attention update, diffusion expressions, and loss definitions remain identical, including Equations 1–4. No assumptions, derivations, formal results, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about multi-entity 6DoF control, entity–trajectory correspondence, dataset construction, generalization, and state-of-the-art accuracy.

C2.justification: Mechanism explanations, quality–accuracy tradeoffs, and limitations remain unchanged. Section 3.3 replaces 'MatrixCity style' with 'UE style', aligning terminology with the UE-style interpretation already explicit in v1 Section 4.6.

D1.justification: Implementation details, hardware, hyperparameters, preprocessing, backbone documentation, evaluation prompts, and project-access information are unchanged across Section 4.1 and the appendices.

R1.justification: Section 2, Appendix B, and the reference list retain the same cited works and research positioning. The relationship to prior 2D motion-control and 3D camera-control methods is unchanged.

P1.justification: The sole body-text wording edit changes 'MatrixCity style' to 'UE style' in Section 3.3. V2 also adds the ICLR 2025 publication header and updates the arXiv stamp; section order and narrative structure remain intact.

P2.justification: V2 adds a conference-publication running header and updates the first-page arXiv stamp. Page 6 has minor paragraph reflow, while all figures, tables, captions, and their placement remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: V2 preserves the scientific content, experimental evidence, limitations, and reproducibility information, including all appendix results. The terminology correction improves local consistency, but it and the publication-header updates do not materially change the paper's overall clarity, rigor, or quality.
